\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{محنت} (mehnat)}{محنت (mehnat)}]{\ur{محنت} (mehnat) — hard work; effort}

\label{lesson:UR-C379-mehnat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a scheme, then the Urdu for to achieve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{محنت}}
\textbf{\ur{محنت}} — \emph{mehnat} — \textquotedblleft{}hard work; effort\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{نے} \ur{محنت} \ur{کی} \ur{تو} \ur{نتیجہ} \ur{اچھا} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum ne mehnat kī to natījā achchhā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you work hard, the result will be good.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{محنت}} (\emph{mehnat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{miḥna}, \textquotedblleft{}a trial, a hardship\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ur{محنتی}}, \textquotedblleft{}hardworking\textquotedblright{}, is built on it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mehnat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mehnat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum ne mehnat kī to natījā achchhā ho gā.} — If you work hard, the result will be good.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a scheme, then the Urdu for to achieve, then say \emph{mehnat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{محنت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hard work; effort\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جوش} (josh)}{جوش (josh)}]{\ur{جوش} (josh) — enthusiasm; fervour}

\label{lesson:UR-C379-josh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to achieve, then the Urdu for hard work.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جوش}}
\textbf{\ur{جوش}} — \emph{josh} — \textquotedblleft{}enthusiasm; fervour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{جوش} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{تھکن} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ہوتی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar josh hai to thakan nahīṅ hotī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you are keen, you do not get tired.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جوش}} (\emph{josh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{josh}, \textquotedblleft{}boiling, ferment\textquotedblright{}: feeling that bubbles up.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لگن} (lagan)}{لگن (lagan)}]{\ur{لگن} (lagan) — dedication; devotion (to a task)}

\label{lesson:UR-C379-lagan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for hard work, then the Urdu for enthusiasm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لگن}}
\textbf{\ur{لگن}} — \emph{lagan} — \textquotedblleft{}dedication; devotion (to a task)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{اس} \ur{میں} \ur{لگن} \ur{ہوتی} \ur{تو} \ur{وہ} \ur{آج} \ur{ماہر} \ur{ہوتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar us meṅ lagan hotī to voh āj māhir hotā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he had been dedicated, he would be an expert today.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لگن}} (\emph{lagan}) is built on \textbf{\ur{لگنا}}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lagnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be attached to\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{lagyati}, \textquotedblleft{}adheres\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10895). Sticking to a task.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مسلسل} (musalsal)}{مسلسل (musalsal)}]{\ur{مسلسل} (musalsal) — continuous; without a break}

\label{lesson:UR-C379-musalsal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for enthusiasm, then the Urdu for dedication.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مسلسل}}
\textbf{\ur{مسلسل}} — \emph{musalsal} — \textquotedblleft{}continuous; without a break\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{مسلسل} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{سیلاب} \ur{آئے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar musalsal bārish huī to sailāb āe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains without a break, there will be a flood.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مسلسل}} (\emph{musalsal}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{musalsal}, \textquotedblleft{}linked like a chain\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دہرانا} (dohrānā)}{دہرانا (dohrānā)}]{\ur{دہرانا} (dohrānā) — to go over again; to repeat}

\label{lesson:UR-C379-dohrana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for dedication, then the Urdu for without a break.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دہرانا}}
\textbf{\ur{دہرانا}} — \emph{dohrānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to go over again; to repeat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{سبق} \ur{دہراؤ} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{یاد} \ur{رہے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum sabaq dohrāo ge to yād rahe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you go over the lesson, you will remember it.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{سبق} \ur{دہرایا}, \emph{us ne sabaq dohrāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دہرانا}} (\emph{dohrānā}) is a verb made on \emph{dohrā}, \textquotedblleft{}double\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{dohrā} under \emph{*dudhāra}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 6407). To do a thing twice over.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dohrānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum sabaq dohrāo ge to yād rahe gā.} — If you go over the lesson, you will remember it.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for dedication, then the Urdu for without a break, then say \emph{dohrānā} again
\end{itemize}
